analyticalQuestion: After resolving one Fourier--Leray triad into its two transverse output polarizations, which channel retains the critical high--high-to-low constant and which channel has a strict separated-cell gap?
supportedClaim: The ordered normalized Fourier--Leray kernel has an exact normal channel with gain g_N=sqrt(1-mu^2), independent of shell separation and capable of attaining one, and an in-plane channel with g_T<=(1+rho)/2<1 when |k|/|p|<=rho<1; the sharp separated in-plane limit is one half, while the normal near-saturation solid-angle fraction sqrt(2 delta-delta^2) does not decay with shell ratio.

chartContract.takeaway: The planar polarization improves under scale separation, but the normal polarization retains the critical constant on a shell-independent positive angular set.
